policy.purpose: Difficulty- and prior-knowledge-aware SBA teaching map between Core1 and Core2.
policy.primary_question_rule: Each Q01-Q59 has exactly one primary SBA bucket.
policy.production_selection_rule: Skip dedicated SBA PDFs when primary question count is zero.
policy.priority_rule: Prioritise D2-D4 buckets for learners at or below 50% usable prior knowledge.
policy.core2_hint_preteach_rule: Every Core2 H1/H2/H3 reveal must trace to earlier Core1A teaching; release prerequisites may delay a question.
policy.teaching_sequence_rule: Pretrain -> visual stages -> physics meaning -> maths -> worked/guided practice -> retrieval -> Core2.

required_support_20pct: full rebuild+staged visual+derivation+multiple examples+guided transfer+hint audit

buckets.learner_title: Use one clock at a special event
buckets.production_reason: Primary Core2 present; timed-event questions require a dedicated 20-percent learner bridge that assembles earlier component and same-height ideas into one-clock routines.

learning_atoms.title: A special event is a snapshot
learning_atoms.purpose: Treat a wall, point P, apex or landing as one instant on the same projectile clock.
teaching_moves: draw one launch-to-landing timeline with marked events
show x and y at one event share the same t
write x_p=u_x t_p and y_p=u_y t_p-1/2 g t_p^2
misconceptions: a named event starts a new projectile
x and y may use different event times
checks: explain why one event needs one shared time

learning_atoms.title: Recover the hidden launch from a timed coordinate
learning_atoms.purpose: Use known x, y and t at one event to recover the initial horizontal and vertical components.
teaching_moves: use u_x=x_p/t_p first
use the same t_p in the vertical event equation
interpret the recovered components as launch-state information
misconceptions: the marked event must be the apex
the horizontal and vertical equations describe different moments
checks: recover u_x and u_y from a fresh timed coordinate

learning_atoms.title: Do not reset the clock after the event
learning_atoms.purpose: Continue the original motion after an intermediate event using T-t_p rather than inventing a second time origin.
teaching_moves: compare one global timeline with a wrong reset-at-event timeline
mark event time t_p and landing time T
write remaining time=T-t_p
misconceptions: set t=0 again after the wall or point P
checks: find remaining time from a total flight time and event time

learning_atoms.title: Same-height landing reveals the total clock
learning_atoms.purpose: Use u_y to recover total flight time when landing returns to the launch level.
teaching_moves: mark launch, apex and landing on one trajectory
restate T=2u_y/g with its validity condition
connect recovered u_y from an event to whole-flight time
checks: state when the same-height total-time shortcut is valid

learning_atoms.title: Build total time from time parts
learning_atoms.purpose: Combine time to an intermediate point and time from that point to landing before doing kinematics.
teaching_moves: draw launch-to-P and P-to-landing intervals on one line
add the two intervals to obtain T
identify which interval is measured from launch
misconceptions: treat the post-P interval as the total flight time
checks: build T correctly from two stated time segments

learning_atoms.title: Use total time to reconstruct event height
learning_atoms.purpose: Convert total same-height flight time to u_y, then evaluate y at the event time measured from launch.
teaching_moves: find u_y=gT/2
return to t=t_to_P
evaluate y=u_y t-1/2 gt^2
misconceptions: use the remaining time after P inside the height equation for P
checks: find event height from a split flight-time description

learning_atoms.title: Use the apex time as a sense check
learning_atoms.purpose: Locate the event before or after the apex using T/2 without replacing the main calculation.
teaching_moves: plot height against time
mark apex at T/2
compare t_p with T/2 to check rising or falling state
misconceptions: treat symmetry as a substitute for the event equations in every case
checks: classify a timed event as rising or falling

learning_atoms.title: Choose the event family before calculating
learning_atoms.purpose: Distinguish timed-coordinate recovery from time-partition reconstruction and select the correct first move.
teaching_moves: compare the two problem families side by side
map recognition signal to first move
complete mixed transfer practice without family labels
misconceptions: choose formulas from keywords without identifying the event information structure
checks: identify the correct first move for Q05-like and Q26-like structures

hint_rungs.evidence: The wall is taught as an intermediate event on one continuous flight rather than as a new launch.
Timed x and y coordinates are used at one shared t to recover u_x and u_y.
Worked and independent practice start with the horizontal event equation to recover u_x first.
Time before P and time after P are explicitly combined into one total flight time.
Same-height total time is converted to u_y and the event height is then evaluated at the launch-based event time.
Worked and independent practice use u_y=gT/2 before substituting t_to_P in the vertical position equation.
